title: team-review workflow concurrency: queue duplicate runs on a repo-wide group instead of cancelling them
answers: Why did a second team-review run get cancelled when the bot's labels were applied twice?
How are concurrent runs of the team-review workflow queued or cancelled?
Where is the concurrency setting for the PR reviewer assignment workflow?
Can I make a workflow that rewrites a shared stats issue run one at a time without losing queued runs?
body:
Path: .github/workflows/team-review.yml (top-level `concurrency:` block) controls how runs of the team-review workflow, which assigns human reviewers to a PR when the `team-review` label is added, are scheduled when several triggers fire close together.
Rule: Keep the concurrency group repo-wide (`group: ${{ github.workflow }}`) because every run rewrites the shared stats issue, and set `queue: max` with `cancel-in-progress: false` so pending runs are queued rather than dropped. A repo-wide group with the default behaviour keeps only one pending run, which silently cancels the others.
Symptom: When the bot's labels were applied twice on a PR, one of the queued team-review runs was cancelled, so reviewers were not assigned in that run and the stats were left inconsistent.
Constraints: Applies to workflows whose runs all write the same shared resource and must not overlap. Do not switch to a per-PR group unless the stats writes are no longer shared.
applies: Concurrency settings of .github/workflows/team-review.yml; relevant to any workflow that serialises writes to a shared repo-level issue.
says: Reviewers were not assigned after the team review label was added multiple times.
Concurrent pull request review requests get silently cancelled instead of being processed.
Team review automation should queue duplicate label events instead of dropping them.
Team reviewer tracking metrics became out of sync after simultaneous pull request updates.
search: In .github/workflows/team-review.yml, configure repo-wide concurrency using group: ${{ github.workflow }}, cancel-in-progress: false, and queue: max. Because every workflow run rewrites a shared repository-level review stats issue, queuing pending runs prevents concurrent executions from cancelling each other, dropping reviewer assignments, and leaving stats inconsistent. This rule applies to workflows serializing writes to a shared repository resource and must not be switched to a per-pull-request group while the stats issue remains shared.
